[gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) shows that negative-sampled BCE can produce overconfidence; its improvements combine generalized BCE with more negatives, so changing both does not isolate the loss effect. Uniform sampled softmax is an established comparator, although its sampled probabilities are not full-softmax probabilities. [eSASRec’s authors](https://github.com/MTSWebServices/RecTools) combine sampled softmax with LiGR Transformer layers, reinforcing the need to separate objective and architecture changes. Keep BCE, gBCE and sampled-softmax alternatives eligible; no paper establishes a universal winner for these four Amazon datasets.

Recommended controlled design: cross the original SASRec block and proposed residual branch with each objective. Hold preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, splits, uniform-negative distribution, negative count, sequence length, masking, batching and evaluation candidates fixed for matched comparisons. Compare losses within each architecture and architectures within each loss; report interactions. Separately vary negative count and gBCE calibration, since these can explain gains. Document softmax temperature and correction conventions. Within 43,200 GPU-seconds, give alternatives comparable tuning budgets, charge failures and diagnostics, and report both validation quality and GPU cost. Equal-update comparisons help attribution; equal-time comparisons measure budget efficiency.

For uncertainty, retain per-user hit indicators and report category HR@10 plus their unweighted macro-average. One hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and the macro by 0.125 points. Use paired, dataset-stratified user bootstrap intervals for macro differences, keeping model outcomes paired. These quantify user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates—not training-seed or candidate-sampling variability. Label conclusions single-seed; report trial count and validation-selection optimism, since ordinary intervals do not correct winner selection. [Sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) warns rankings can differ from full-catalog rankings: preserve the pinned evaluator and describe results specifically as HR@10 against 99 fixed negatives.
